Alice Chen: Hi team — auditor asked for evidence that ephemeral KMS keys used for session tokens are rotated and that those rotations are logged and mapped to SOC2/ISO controls. They want: key rotation events, who requested, approval trail for emergency admin grants, and a short chain-of-custody for decrypt permissions. Can we assemble?
Ben Ortega: Yep. We rotate ephemeral keys via the key-versioning flow. Cloud audit logs record CreateCryptoKeyVersion and DestroyCryptoKeyVersion. Also log entry shows caller identity (service account).
Claire Martins: For RBAC changes: we have the RFC/PR in GitHub + Ops ticket in Jira for emergency grants. Approval comments are in the ticket and we have Slack approvals stapled as links. Need to know which time window the auditor wants.
Alice Chen: Auditor wants mapping to SOC2 CC6 (change management) and ISO 27001 A.9/A.12 entries. Also they asked for evidence that during incident IR-2026-03 we used ephemeral keys and didn't expose long-lived keys.
Ben Ortega: I'll export the audit-log slice. Quick Splunk query I plan to run: ```index=cloud_audit proto=cloudkms resource.type=crypto_key (protoPayload.methodName=CreateCryptoKeyVersion OR protoPayload.methodName=DestroyCryptoKeyVersion) | table _time, protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, resource.labels.key_id, protoPayload.methodName, jsonPayload.request.reason``` That will get timestamps + caller.
Claire Martins: I'll pull the Jira ticket history and approval emails. For emergency admin grants we use temporary role-binding via terraform-apply with approved PR. We can include the PR diff + reviewer comments.
Jane (Auditor): Helpful. For chain-of-custody I need: service account names that had Decrypt/Encrypt during the incident window, IAAS region, and an export showing those service accounts' role binding changes (who granted, time, justification). Also confirm whether any manual key material export happened.
Ben Ortega: There was no key material export — Cloud KMS doesn't allow plaintext export for our key ring. I'll include the 'no-export' proof: cloudkms list-key-rings and the policy-binding snapshot plus a note from the HSM KMS provider.
SecurityBot: Export job started: /s3-compliance-exports/2026-03-24/ir-2026-03-kms-logs.tar.gz (ETA 12m) :white_check_mark:
Alice Chen: Great. Claire/Ben — can you both drop the artifacts into the compliance bundle folder and add a README mapping each file to the control(s)? Use naming: ir2026_kms_logs.csv, ir2026_rbac_jira.pdf, ir2026_pr_diff.txt, ir2026_chain_of_custody.md
Claire Martins: On it. I'll include ticket links and the approver emails and a short statement: "Emergency grant was authorized per oncall runbook v1.4; PR #842 approved by SRE leads."
Ben Ortega: Will attach the Splunk export + raw audit logs and a short script we used to redact PII. Also add proof of key-version creation events and corresponding service account callers.
Jane (Auditor): Thanks — can you mark which files are the canonical evidence for SOC2 CC6 and ISO A.9? Prefer bullets in readme.
Alice Chen: Yes — we'll add an index.md mapping each artifact to control IDs and include exact queries/commands used to generate them. I'll aim to have draft bundle ready by EOD PST.
Claire Martins: ETA EOD PST from me too. If we hit blockers I'll flag here.
Ben Ortega: ETA +1h for log export, +4h for processed CSVs.
Jane (Auditor): Appreciate it. If you can include MD5 hashes for the exported tarball and a signed note (ops lead) that would be ideal.
Alice Chen: Noted — will get ops lead signoff in the README. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
